_howTo: Edit this file, or use the admin page (the small dot at the bottom of the site), to update the Calendar and Events page. "date" (YYYY-MM-DD) puts an event on that day; "month" (YYYY-MM) lists it under dates to be announced. "time", "location" and "description" are optional (the description is the short text on the calendar). Optional extras for the Events page: "details" (the full write-up: blank line between paragraphs, lines starting with "- " make a list, [text](https://link) makes a link, **bold** makes bold text) and "images" (a list of {src, caption, alt}). If "details" is set the Events page shows it exactly as written; otherwise it shows the description plus time and location. Add "hideOnEventsPage": true to keep an event on the calendar only.

events.title: Kickoff Event
events.description: A mini conference to kick off McMaster AIAA. Learn from industry professionals from NASA and Bombardier and hear directly from people working in aerospace.
events.details:
We hosted our very first kickoff event for the McMaster AIAA Student Branch, welcoming students to hear firsthand perspectives on space exploration and the aerospace industry, while connecting with professionals in the field.

- [Alice Bowman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alice-bowman-63279169/), Mission Operations Manager for NASA’s New Horizons mission, took us through the journey of the New Horizons space probe, what lies ahead for the mission, and the challenges of operating a spacecraft billions of kilometres from Earth.
- [Stephen Carnduff](https://www.linkedin.com/in/stephen-carnduff-0bb1062a/), Technical Expert in Stability & Control at Bombardier, walked us through the supersonic flight-testing program for the Global 8000 and explored why the aircraft had to be pushed beyond Mach 1.
- We also thank [Walter Gordon](https://www.linkedin.com/in/walter-gordon-a7849538/), Chairman of the AIAA Niagara Frontier Section and former development manager and engineer with Moog Space and Defense Group, for joining us and helping make this event possible.

Thank you to our speakers, our executive team, and everyone who came out and helped make our first major event a success. Stay tuned for what’s ahead for McMaster AIAA!

events.title: Workshop 01: Foamboard Glider
events.description: Learn the basics of aerodynamics, design and build your own glider, and put it to the test in a flight-distance competition. No experience needed. Limited spots, so register through the link in our Instagram bio.
events.details:
Learn and explore the fundamentals of aerodynamics, incuding lift, drag, stability, and wing design! 

Work in teams of 3-4 to design and construct your own foamboard glider. Experiment with different wing shapes, stabilizer designs, and placements with a foamboard fuselage!

Put your glider to the test in a flight-distance competition! See how your wing designs perform and compete for the longest flight.

No experience needed!

events.title: Aerospace Trivia Night
events.description:
Join us for a fun, Jeopardy-style trivia night covering space exploration, aircraft, aerospace history, pop culture, and more!

Compete in small teams across two trivia rounds, chances to win fun prizes! No prior aerospace knowledge needed - everyone is welcome!

events.title: Workshop 02: Parachute Drop Challenge
events.description: Work in groups of 3-4 to build your own parachute! Feel free to bring your friends! Learn about drag force and terminal velocity, and explain how parachute geometry affects descent rate!
events.details:
Work in groups of 3-4 to build your own parachute! Feel free to bring your friends! 
- Learn about drag force and terminal velocity, and explain how parachute geometry affects descent rate! 
- Choose materials by weighting weight, drag, and durability trade-offs
- Run the full engineering design process in one session! 
[Sign up!](https://tr.ee/zpaDPQHIeo)
